title: The Day God Ordered Pizza
summary: A character-driven puzzle adventure with an intentionally unusual premise.
description: A game project combining interaction design, narrative systems, level logic and supporting API experiments.

blocks.text:
The Day God Ordered Pizza (TDGOP) is a First Person Puzzle Adventure title set in a hilarious fictional world with a beautifully hand drawn art style.

The story begins with you (the main character) working at a pizza restaurant and getting a phone call from God who then proceeds to order a Pizza from you. Upon attempting to deliver the pizza, you are hit by a car and find yourself waking up in a bizarre universe filled with larger than life characters, intense but intuitive puzzles and a story with a great twist.

Elevator Ego has an extremely expressive dialogue system given the limitations of the art style. We use this to effectively communicate emotion to the player.
The dialogue system is effectively 2 parts.

The first half of the equation is the text boxes. This game has no traditional voice acting, so we needed to explore the expression of dialogue through text. This posed quite a large challenge as players do not typically enjoy reading walls of text. To combat this, we implemented a feature where we can animate and colour specific words so that skimming the text or reading very quickly will still provide the needed information to further the story or solve a puzzle. This combined with the simplification of dialogue not only solved the problem we initially had but had the added benefit of making the text fun to read and very interactive.

The second half of the expressive dialogue dilemma comes from character expressions. Now that our text is fun to read, it was time to convey the emotion of the text through character expressions. This was quite a difficult solution to properly implement, having to worry about the timing of mouth changes for words, and facial expression changes based on the context of the dialogue.

These two systems combined formed the basis of our unique dialogue system as shown below.

This game is very heavily focussed on story, dialogue, interactions and puzzles.

Despite the cartoon aesthetic, we really wanted to create a compelling story that would immediately engage the player and keep them entertained throughout.

Between the moments of the main story, we felt it to be very important to make the world feel authentic. Puzzles are normally something that feel nice to complete but a little detatched from the world they're in and we wanted to avoid this feeling so we have made a large effort to weave the puzzles into side stories between NPC's.

These NPC's have their own agenda and motives but reward you for completing a task for them. This model felt like the best way to implement puzzles into the project so that as the player explores and discovers new characters in the world, they may also be uncovering clues to a puzzle that they need to complete in order to progress.

This allowed our puzzles to feel organic and real. The player isn't just pushing buttons in an empty room, they're helping an NPC listen to a vinyl that they've been unable to listen to for years (in this case because they're a portrait on a wall). Or help 2 sisters obtain an old family photo.

Framing our puzzles in this way is how we acheive a sense of cohesion and seamlessness.

The project is in active development so the contents of videos and screenshots may change upon final release.
Here is a short demonstration of the alpha build intro to the game.

title: Boids System
description: A real-time visual experiment modelling flocking, schooling and organic group movement.

blocks.text:
This is a simple demonstration of a boids system. This system is used generally to create flocks of birds and to mimic real world behaviour of flocking animals. In this example I used the system to create organic feeling schools of fish. Approaching fish in this way allowed me to create something that felt very natural all while being immensely less resource intensive and time intensive than creating animations by hand with the added benefit of the behaviours being dynamic.

This is a preview of the system in development.
Here is an example of the system used in game.

title: The Day God Ordered Pizza API
summary: A supporting API designed around the systems used by the game project.
description: An API experiment accompanying The Day God Ordered Pizza.

blocks.text:
This is a demonstration of the API I created to interface with The Day God Ordered Pizza.

In the game, there are multiple scenarios where the player is able to input their name or a message. This will then be uploaded and saved to a database. When another player is in that same scenario, they may see the original players name or message.
The uploading and downloading of data all happens in the background while the player continues their journey.

Although there are a number of third party solutions to help achieve this, I found they left a lot to be desired and would restrict what data we are able to save. As a result, I decided to create my own solution so that it could be tailored to the needs of the game and was scalable.

My method was quite simple in design although did require experience with SQL, PHP and web development.

The process is as follows; Set up an SQL Server with predefined tables. Create a simple web interface in PHP that can interpret results from a query string and use them to insert data into the database. Create a secondary web page that can return results from the database using the parameters of the query string.

With this now set up on a server I am able to query a specific webpage with a query string that is built inside Unity which will allow me to either insert or return data to/from the database.
The query string is dynamically built and interpreted by the API as to then create a dynamic SQL query.

Funkyball is a passion project I worked on in my spare time in an attempt to recreate an old flash game I played endlessly when I was younger.

This is a simple 2D game where you control a ball and navigate platforms and obstacles in order to reach a goal.
Once the goal is reached, your time on the level is saved and you progress to the next stage.

The levels get progressively more challenging as you play leading to an addictive and unique platforming experience.

The game features a character selection system where skins for your ball are unlocked through level progression along side an online leader board which displays your overall time, the skin you are currently using and a display name.

This project is due to be released on itch.io for free once the visual style has been perfected.
